To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the RTQ 5 and PTQ have a unidimensional structure and are good transdiagnostic measures; 2) the RTQ and PTQ are associated with depression and anxiety, and the PTQ is also associated with mania; 3) the RPA has three factors and is a good transdiagnostic measure; 4) the RNT and RPT factors of the RPA have unique relationships with emotional symptoms.

repetitive negative thinking (RTN) and repetitive positive thinking (RPT) are distinct cognitive processes, both of which are transdiagnostic and associated with emotional symptoms, but with unique associations.
transdiagnostic assessment of RNT and RPT is useful in predicting emotional disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive processes that are central to the development and maintenance of emotional disorders.
the role of repetitive thinking in the onset and maintenance of emotional disorders.
the role of repetitive negative thinking (R NT) in the maintenance of emotional disorders, and with the development of transdiagnostic measures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

RNT and RPT are transdiagnostic processes that have unique predictive utility for emotional disorder symptoms, and that the PTQ and RTQ 10 measure RNT whereas the RPA dampening subscale is a unique process.

repetitive negative thinking (RPT), as measured by the Perseverative Thought Questionnaire (PT) and repetitive positive thinking, as measured by the Responses to Positive affect (RPA), are transdiagnostic constructs that are uniquely predictive of emotional symptoms.
RNT has a strong relationship with anxiety and depression, whereas RPA has a strong relationship specifically with mania symptoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
repetitive positive thinking and repetitive negative thinking are distinct processes that contribute to emotional symptoms.
the RPA dampening subscale may be a promising transdiagnostic marker for anxiety and depression symptoms.
repetitive negative thinking is a common factor in the development of emotional disorders, and repetitive positive thinking is a specific risk factor for bipolar disorder.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transdiagnostic measures we examined are essentially unidirectional, and that the RPA is a multidimensional scale.
RPA is a unique process that is not captured by existing RNT measures. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2020 APA, all rights reserved)
